key_insight: A diffusion-based generative model can reconstruct city-scale air pollution fields from sparse station readings and better preserve realistic spatial structure than purely deterministic approaches.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more reliable urban air-quality mapping for exposure assessment, public health monitoring, and deployment in sensor-limited cities.
method: Trains deep learning models on full-field air-quality simulation data for NO2, O3, PM2.5, and PM10.
Benchmarks deterministic reconstruction models against a diffusion-based generative framework.
Uses data augmentation to transfer models to real-world Paris observations without retraining.
evidence_signal: Models were evaluated on Paris observations from 9 to 28 monitoring stations and showed high structural similarity on simulated validation data plus realistic spatial patterns on real observations, supported by power-spectrum analysis.
watch_item: Generalization to operational use may still depend on station coverage, observation noise, and how well simulation-trained models match the target city's meteorology and emission patterns.
paper_title: From Deterministic to Generative Deep Learning for Urban Air Quality Reconstruction from Sparse Observations
